registryLegalName: Removal of a Record from the Central Repository After a Favourable Disposition (NRS 179A.160)

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Where a person is acquitted or the disposition of the charge is favourable to the person, that person may apply in writing to the Central Repository and to the agency which maintains the record to have it removed from the files that are available and generally searched. Removal is mandatory unless one of the five stated exclusions applies.

verificationStatute.description: NRS 179A.160 is not a court filing and no verification statute applies to it. The required contents and form of the written application are not established by the source; nothing is filled.

presentation.verificationPenaltyLabel: the penalties for a false statement

counselFlags: Record sealing, never expungement. The Nevada Department of Public Safety states directly that sealing is not expungement because it does not authorise destruction of the records.
Sealing does not restore firearm rights. Only a pardon that does not restrict the right to bear arms does.
Nevada orders do not bind out-of-state agencies and do not reach federal, tribal, military or out-of-state records.

Waiting period: none. NRS 179A.160(1) permits the application at any time after the charge is dismissed, acquittal is entered, or disposition of the charge in favour of the person is final. The only temporal condition is that the favourable disposition be final.
Fee: the source establishes no fee for an NRS 179A.160 application to the Central Repository and the record-holding agency. No amount may be stated to a participant.
NRS 179A.160 is not a court filing and no verification statute applies to it. The required contents and form of the written application are not established by the source; nothing is filled.

Route separation: this is a repository remedy, not a court sealing order. It sits alongside the NRS 179.255 petition rather than replacing it, and NRS 179A.160(3) preserves a court's separate authority to order deletion or modification of a record. A participant may need both.

Deferred dispositions defeat this route: NRS 179A.160(2)(c) excludes a deferred prosecution, plea bargain or other similar disposition. This is the exclusion that most often defeats the route in practice, and a participant whose case was resolved by a deferral of judgment belongs on the NRS 176.211 track instead.
The exclusion for a prior felony or gross misdemeanour conviction under NRS 179A.160(2)(d) reaches convictions in any jurisdiction in the United States, not merely in Nevada.

registryExcerpt.legalName: Removal of a Record from the Central Repository After a Favourable Disposition (NRS 179A.160)
registryExcerpt.publicName: Getting a Nevada arrest off the state repository after a favourable outcome
registryExcerpt.venue: Not a filing route. The court or agency that handled the matter holds the record.
registryExcerpt.destinationName: The Central Repository for Nevada Records of Criminal History, and the agency which maintains the record

waitingPeriods.condition: None. NRS 179A.160(1) permits the application "at any time after the charge is dismissed, acquittal is entered or disposition of the charge in favor of the person is final". The only temporal condition is that the favourable disposition be final.

exclusions: NRS 179A.160(2)(a): the person is a fugitive.
NRS 179A.160(2)(b): the case is under active prosecution according to a current certificate of a prosecuting attorney.

NRS 179A.160(2)(c): the disposition of the case was a deferred prosecution, plea bargain or other similar disposition. This is the exclusion that most often defeats the route in practice and it is why a participant whose case was resolved by a deferral of judgment belongs on the NRS 176.211 track and not here.
NRS 179A.160(2)(d): the person has a prior conviction for a felony or gross misdemeanour in any jurisdiction in the United States — not merely in Nevada.
NRS 179A.160(2)(e): the person has been arrested for or charged with another crime, other than a minor traffic violation, since the arrest, citation or warrant which the person seeks to have removed.

caption.detail: Blocked as a pleading: NRS 179A.160 is not a filing route. The remedy is a written application made by the subject of the record to two agency recipients — the Central Repository for Nevada Records of Criminal History and the agency which maintains the record. It is not a court filing, no order issues on it, and it does not reach the court's own record.

dependencies.exactMissingSource: The required contents, format and any prescribed wording of the NRS 179A.160(1) written application. The committed Nevada evidence names the document role (nv_favorable_disposition_repository_request) but commits no application text, no form and no prescribed contents. Registry venue field reads 'Not a filing route. The court or agency that handled the matter holds the record.'
dependencies.barsDraftingBecause: The controlled custom-pleading renderer produces a court caption, jurisdiction and venue allegations, a prayer for relief addressed to a court, and a proposed order for a judge's signature. None of those exist on this route. Rendering them would fabricate a court proceeding that NRS 179A.160 does not create.
